question: Find the settlement amount of the claim with the largest claim amount. Show both the settlement amount and claim amount.

sql.W1:
SELECT T1.Amount_Settled, T1.Amount_Claimed
FROM Settlements T1
JOIN (
    SELECT Claim_ID, MAX(Amount_Claimed) AS MaxClaimAmount
    FROM Settlements
    GROUP BY Claim_ID
) T2
ON T1.Claim_ID = T2.Claim_ID AND T1.Amount_Claimed = T2.MaxClaimAmount
sql.W2:
SELECT S.Amount_Settled, C.Amount_Claimed
FROM Settlements S
JOIN Claims C ON S.Claim_ID = C.Claim_ID
WHERE C.Amount_Claimed = (
    SELECT MAX(Amount_Claimed)
    FROM Claims
)
ORDER BY S.Amount_Settled DESC LIMIT 1
sql.W3:
SELECT S.Amount_Settled, C.Amount_Claimed
FROM Settlements S
JOIN Claims C ON S.Claim_ID = C.Claim_ID
WHERE C.Amount_Claimed = (
    SELECT MAX(Amount_Claimed)
    FROM Claims
)
ORDER BY S.Amount_Settled DESC LIMIT 1
sql.W4: SELECT T2.Amount_Settled, T1.Amount_Claimed FROM Claims AS T1 JOIN Settlements AS T2 ON T1.Claim_ID = T2.Claim_ID ORDER BY T1.Amount_Claimed DESC LIMIT 1
sql.E:
SELECT T1.Amount_Settled, T1.Amount_Claimed
FROM Settlements T1
JOIN Claims T2 ON T1.Claim_ID = T2.Claim_ID
ORDER BY T1.Amount_Claimed DESC
LIMIT 1

question: List the themes of parties in ascending order of number of hosts.

sql.W1: SELECT Party_Theme FROM party ORDER BY Number_of_hosts ASC
sql.W2:
SELECT p.Party_Theme 
FROM party p 
JOIN party_host ph ON p.Party_ID = ph.Party_ID 
GROUP BY p.Party_ID 
ORDER BY COUNT(ph.Host_ID) ASC
sql.W3:
SELECT p.Party_Theme 
FROM party p 
JOIN party_host ph ON p.Party_ID = ph.Party_ID 
GROUP BY p.Party_ID 
ORDER BY COUNT(ph.Host_ID) ASC
sql.W4:
SELECT p.Party_Theme 
FROM party p 
JOIN party_host ph ON p.Party_ID = ph.Party_ID 
GROUP BY p.Party_ID 
ORDER BY SUM(CASE WHEN ph.Is_Main_in_Charge = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC 
LIMIT (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Party_ID) FROM party_host)
sql.E: SELECT Party_Theme FROM party ORDER BY Number_of_hosts ASC

question: When are the birthdays of customer who are classified as 'Good Customer' status?

sql.W1:
SELECT first_name, last_name, date_of_birth 
FROM Customers 
WHERE customer_status_code = 'Good Customer' AND date_of_birth IS NOT NULL
sql.W2:
SELECT DISTINCT c.first_name, c.last_name, c.date_of_birth 
FROM Customers c
JOIN Customer_Status cs ON c.customer_status_code = cs.customer_status_code
WHERE cs.customer_status_code = 'Good Customer' AND c.date_of_birth IS NOT NULL
sql.W3:
SELECT DISTINCT c.first_name, c.last_name, c.date_of_birth 
FROM Customers c
JOIN Customer_Status cs ON c.customer_status_code = cs.customer_status_code
WHERE cs.customer_status_code = 'Good Customer' AND c.date_of_birth IS NOT NULL
sql.W4: SELECT T3.first_name, T3.last_name, T3.date_of_birth FROM Customers AS T3 JOIN Customer_Payments AS T4 ON T3.customer_id = T4.customer_id WHERE T3.customer_status_code = 'Good Customer' AND T3.date_of_birth IS NOT NULL
sql.E:
SELECT DISTINCT c.first_name, c.last_name, c.date_of_birth 
FROM Customers c 
JOIN Customer_Payments cp ON c.customer_id = cp.customer_id 
WHERE c.customer_status_code = 'Good Customer' AND c.date_of_birth <= DATE('now') AND c.date_of_birth + INTERVAL 1 YEAR >= DATE('now')

question: Return the hispanic percentage for cities in which the black percentage is greater than 10.

sql.W1:
SELECT (Hispanic * 100) / (White + Black + Amerindian + Asian + Multiracial + Hispanic) AS Hispanic_Percentage
FROM city
WHERE Black > 10
sql.W2:
SELECT c.Name, (c.Hispanic * 100 / NULLIF(c.Black, 0)) AS Hispanic_Percentage
FROM city c
WHERE c.Black > 10
GROUP BY c.Name
sql.W3:
SELECT c.Name, (c.Hispanic * 100 / NULLIF((c.White + c.Black + c.Amerindian + c.Asian + c.Multiracial), 0)) AS Hispanic_Percentage
FROM city c
WHERE c.Black > 10
GROUP BY c.Name
sql.W4:
SELECT CAST(Hispanic AS REAL) * 100 / (White + Black + Amerindian + Asian + Multiracial + Hispanic) AS Hispanic_Percentage
FROM city
WHERE Black > 10
JOIN county_public_safety ON city.County_ID = county_public_safety.County_ID
sql.E:
SELECT c.Name, (c.Hispanic * 100 / NULLIF((c.White + c.Black + c.Amerindian + c.Asian + c.Multiracial), 0)) AS Hispanic_Percentage
FROM city c
WHERE c.Black > 10
GROUP BY c.Name

question: Find the name of the document that has been accessed the greatest number of times, as well as the count of how many times it has been accessed?

LIMIT 1

LIMIT 1

FROM Documents d

) subq ON d.document_code = subq.document_code

question: Among all the claims, what is the settlement amount of the claim with the largest claim amount? List both the settlement amount and claim amount.

sql.W1:
SELECT T1.Amount_Settled, T1.Amount_Claimed
FROM Settlements T1
JOIN (
    SELECT Claim_ID, MAX(Amount_Claimed) AS MaxClaimAmount
    FROM Settlements
    GROUP BY Claim_ID
) T2
ON T1.Claim_ID = T2.Claim_ID AND T1.Amount_Claimed = T2.MaxClaimAmount
sql.W2:
SELECT T1.Amount_Settled, T1.Amount_Claimed 
FROM Settlements AS T1 
JOIN Claims AS T2 ON T1.Claim_ID = T2.Claim_ID 
WHERE T1.Amount_Claimed = (SELECT MAX(Amount_Claimed) FROM Claims) 
LIMIT 1
sql.W3:
SELECT T1.Amount_Settled, T1.Amount_Claimed 
FROM Settlements AS T1 
JOIN Claims AS T2 ON T1.Claim_ID = T2.Claim_ID 
WHERE T1.Amount_Claimed = (SELECT MAX(Amount_Claimed) FROM Claims) 
LIMIT 1
sql.W4:
SELECT T2.Amount_Settled, T1.Amount_Claimed 
FROM Claims AS T1 
JOIN Settlements AS T2 ON T1.Claim_ID = T2.Claim_ID 
WHERE T1.Amount_Claimed = (SELECT MAX(Amount_Claimed) FROM Claims)
sql.E:
SELECT T1.Amount_Settled, T1.Amount_Claimed 
FROM Claims AS T1 
JOIN Settlements AS T2 ON T1.Claim_ID = T2.Claim_ID 
WHERE T1.Amount_Claimed = (SELECT MAX(Amount_Claimed) FROM Claims) 
ORDER BY T1.Amount_Claimed DESC LIMIT 1

question: In February, which city marks the highest temperature?

ORDER BY Highest_Temperature DESC
LIMIT 1

ORDER BY Highest_Feb_Temperature DESC
LIMIT 1

question: For all directors who directed more than one movie, return the titles of all movies directed by them, along with the director name. Sort by director name, then movie title.

sql.W1:
SELECT director, GROUP_CONCAT(title ORDER BY title) AS movies
FROM Movie
GROUP BY director
HAVING COUNT(mID) > 1
ORDER BY director, title
sql.W2:
SELECT M.director, R.title
FROM Movie M
JOIN (
    SELECT mID, COUNT(*) AS movieCount
    FROM Movie
    GROUP BY mID
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
) MM ON M.mID = MM.mID
JOIN Movie R ON MM.mID = R.mID
JOIN Reviewer V ON M.director = V.name
ORDER BY V.name, R.title
sql.W3:
SELECT M.director, R.title
FROM Movie M
JOIN (
    SELECT mID, COUNT(*) AS movieCount
    FROM Movie
    GROUP BY mID
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
) MM ON M.mID = MM.mID
JOIN Movie R ON MM.mID = R.mID
JOIN Reviewer V ON M.director = V.name
ORDER BY V.name, R.title
sql.W4:
SELECT M.title, R.name 
FROM Movie M 
JOIN Rating R ON M.mID = R.mID 
JOIN Reviewer R2 ON R.rID = R2.rID 
GROUP BY M.director, M.title 
HAVING COUNT(M.mID) > 1 
ORDER BY R2.name, M.title
sql.E:
SELECT director, GROUP_CONCAT(title ORDER BY title) AS movies
FROM Movie
GROUP BY director
HAVING COUNT(mID) > 1
ORDER BY director, title

SELECT s.building, s.room_number, s.semester, s.year 
FROM section s
JOIN course c ON s.course_id = c.course_id
WHERE c.dept_name = 'Psychology'
ORDER BY c.title

WHERE c.dept_name = 'Psychology'

FROM course AS T1 
JOIN section AS T2 ON T1.course_id = T2.course_id 
JOIN teaches AS T4 ON T1.course_id = T4.course_id AND T2.sec_id = T4.sec_id 
JOIN instructor AS T5 ON T4.ID = T5.ID 
JOIN department AS T6 ON T5.dept_name = T6.de
sql.E:
SELECT s.building, s.room_number, s.semester, s.year 
FROM section s
JOIN course c ON s.course_id = c.course_id
JOIN department d ON c.dept_name = d.dept_name
WHERE d.dept_name = 'Psychology'
ORDER BY c.title

question: Find the total checking and saving balance of all accounts sorted by the total balance in ascending order.

sql.W1: SELECT custid, SUM(balance) AS total_balance FROM CHECKING JOIN ACCOUNTS ON CHECKING.custid = ACCOUNTS.custid GROUP BY custid ORDER BY total_balance ASC
sql.W2:
SELECT 
   (accounts.custid, SUM(checking.balance)) AS total_checking,
   (accounts.custid, SUM(savings.balance)) AS total_savings
FROM 
   CHECKING
JOIN 
   ACCOUNTS ON CHECKING.custid = ACCOUNTS.custid
JOIN 
   SAVINGS ON ACCOUNTS.custid = SAVINGS.custid
GROUP BY 
   accounts.custid
ORDER BY 
   total_checking + total_savings
sql.W3:
SELECT 
   (accounts.custid, SUM(checking.balance)) AS total_checking,
   (accounts.custid, SUM(savings.balance)) AS total_savings
FROM 
   CHECKING
JOIN 
   ACCOUNTS ON CHECKING.custid = ACCOUNTS.custid
JOIN 
   SAVINGS ON ACCOUNTS.custid = SAVINGS.custid
GROUP BY 
   accounts.custid
ORDER BY 
   total_checking + total_savings
sql.W4:
SELECT 
   custid, 
   (CHECKING.balance + SAVINGS.balance) AS total_balance
FROM 
   ACCOUNTS
JOIN 
   CHECKING ON ACCOUNTS.custid = CHECKING.custid
JOIN 
   SAVINGS ON ACCOUNTS.custid = SAVINGS.custid
ORDER BY 
   total_balance ASC
sql.E: SELECT custid, SUM(balance) AS total_balance FROM CHECKING JOIN ACCOUNTS ON CHECKING.custid = ACCOUNTS.custid GROUP BY custid ORDER BY total_balance ASC

JOIN Director D ON R.rID = D.dID

JOIN Reviewer R ON T.rID = R.rID

question: Find the name of the products that have the color description "red" and have the characteristic name "fast".

question: Find out the send dates of the documents with the grant amount of more than 5000 were granted by organisation type described

FROM Documents D

)

question: What are the names of customers who have a savings balance lower than their checking balance, and what is the total of their checking and savings balances?

sql.W1:
SELECT T1.name, (T1.checking + T2.balance) AS total_balance
FROM ACCOUNTS AS T1
JOIN SAVINGS AS T2 ON T1.custid = T2.custid
WHERE T1.checking > T2.balance

FROM ACCOUNTS A
JOIN SAVINGS S ON A.custid = S.custid
JOIN CHECKING C ON A.custid = C.custid
WHERE S.balance < C.balance
sql.W3:

FROM ACCOUNTS A
JOIN SAVINGS S ON A.custid = S.custid
JOIN CHECKING C ON A.custid = C.custid
WHERE S.balance < C.balance
sql.W4:
SELECT A.name, SUM(S.balance + C.balance) AS Total_Balances
FROM ACCOUNTS A
JOIN SAVINGS S ON A.custid = S.custid
JOIN CHECKING C ON A.custid = C.custid
WHERE S.balance < C.balance
GROUP BY A.name
sql.E:
SELECT T1.name, (T1.checking + T2.balance) AS total_balance
FROM ACCOUNTS AS T1
JOIN SAVINGS AS T2 ON T1.custid = T2.custid
WHERE T1.checking > T2.balance

question: Find the name and total checking and savings balance of the accounts whose savings balance is lower than corresponding checking balance.

sql.W1:
SELECT A.name, (C.balance + S.balance) AS total_balance
FROM ACCOUNTS A
LEFT JOIN CHECKING C ON A.custid = C.custid
LEFT JOIN SAVINGS S ON A.custid = S.custid
WHERE S.balance < C.balance
sql.W2:
SELECT A.name, (C.balance + S.balance) AS total_balance
FROM ACCOUNTS A
JOIN CHECKING C ON A.custid = C.custid
JOIN SAVINGS S ON A.custid = S.custid
WHERE C.balance > S.balance
sql.W3:
SELECT A.name, (C.balance + S.balance) AS total_balance
FROM ACCOUNTS A
JOIN CHECKING C ON A.custid = C.custid
JOIN SAVINGS S ON A.custid = S.custid
WHERE C.balance > S.balance
sql.W4:
SELECT A.name, COALESCE(S.balance + C.balance, 0) AS total_balance
FROM ACCOUNTS A
LEFT JOIN SAVINGS S ON A.custid = S.custid
LEFT JOIN CHECKING C ON A.custid = C.custid
WHERE S.balance < C.balance
sql.E:
SELECT A.name, (C.balance + S.balance) AS total_balance
FROM ACCOUNTS A
LEFT JOIN CHECKING C ON A.custid = C.custid
LEFT JOIN SAVINGS S ON A.custid = S.custid
WHERE S.balance < C.balance

question: For each tourist attraction, return its name and the date when the tourists named Vincent or Vivian visited there.

sql.W1:
SELECT TA.Tourist_Attraction_Name, V.Visit_Date
FROM Visits V
JOIN Tourist_Attractions TA ON V.Tourist_Attraction_ID = TA.Tourist_Attraction_ID
JOIN Visitors Vt ON V.Tourist_ID = Vt.Tourist_ID
WHERE Vt.Tourist_Name IN ('Vincent', 'Vivian')
GROUP BY TA.Tourist_Attraction_Name, V.Visit_Date
sql.W2:
SELECT TA.Name, V.Visit_Date
FROM Visits V
JOIN Tourist_Attractions TA ON V.Tourist_Attraction_ID = TA.Tourist_Attraction_ID
WHERE V.Tourist_ID IN (
    SELECT Visitor_ID FROM Visitors WHERE Tourist_Details LIKE '%Vincent%'
    UNION
    SELECT Visitor_ID FROM Visitors WHERE Tourist_Details LIKE '%Vivian%'
)
sql.W3:
SELECT TA.Name, V.Visit_Date
FROM Visits V
JOIN Tourist_Attractions TA ON V.Tourist_Attraction_ID = TA.Tourist_Attraction_ID
WHERE V.Tourist_ID IN (
    SELECT Visitor_ID FROM Visitors WHERE Tourist_Details LIKE '%Vincent%'
    UNION
    SELECT Visitor_ID FROM Visitors WHERE Tourist_Details LIKE '%Vivian%'
)
sql.W4:
SELECT TA.Name, V.Visit_Date
FROM Tourist_Attractions TA
JOIN Visits V ON TA.Tourist_Attraction_ID = V.Tourist_Attracton_ID
JOIN Visitors Vist ON V.Tourist_ID = Vist.Tourist_ID
WHERE Vist.Name IN ('Vincent', 'Vivian')
sql.E:
SELECT TA.Name, V.Visit_Date
FROM Visits V
JOIN Tourist_Attractions TA ON V.Tourist_Attraction_ID = TA.Tourist_Attraction_ID
JOIN Visitors VD ON V.Tourist_ID = VD.Tourist_ID
WHERE VD.Name IN ('Vincent', 'Vivian')
GROUP BY TA.Name, V.Visit_Date

question: Which customers have used the service named "Close a policy" or "Upgrade a policy"? Give me the customer names.

sql.W1: SELECT DISTINCT c.Name FROM Customers c JOIN Customers_Policies cp ON c.Customer_ID = cp.Customer_ID WHERE cp.Date_Closed IS NOT NULL OR cp.Policy_ID IN (SELECT Policy_ID FROM Available_Policies WHERE Policy_Name IN ("Upgrade a policy", "Close a policy"))
sql.W2:
SELECT C.Customer_name FROM Customers AS C JOIN Customers_Policies AS CP ON C.Customer_ID = CP.Customer_ID WHERE CP.Date_Closed IS NOT NULL OR CP.Date_Closed IS NULL AND CP.Policy_ID IN (
    SELECT A.Policy_ID FROM Available_Policies AS A JOIN First_Notification_of_Loss AS FNL ON A.Policy_ID = FNL.Policy_ID WHERE FNL.Service_ID IN (SELECT Service_ID FROM Services WHERE Service_name IN ('Close a policy', 'Upgrade
sql.W3:
SELECT C.Customer_name FROM Customers AS C JOIN Customers_Policies AS CP ON C.Customer_ID = CP.Customer_ID WHERE CP.Date_Closed IS NOT NULL OR CP.Date_Closed IS NULL AND CP.Policy_ID IN (
    SELECT A.Policy_ID FROM Available_Policies AS A JOIN First_Notification_of_Loss AS FNL ON A.Policy_ID = FNL.Policy_ID WHERE FNL.Service_ID IN (SELECT Service_ID FROM Services WHERE Service_name IN ('Close a policy', 'Upgrade
sql.W4:
SELECT DISTINCT c.Customer_name
FROM Customers c
JOIN Customers_Policies cp ON c.Customer_ID = cp.Customer_ID
JOIN Available_Policies ap ON cp.Policy_ID = ap.Policy_ID
JOIN First_Notification_of_Loss fnol ON cp.Customer_ID = fnol.Customer_ID AND cp.Policy_ID = fnol.Policy_ID

WHERE s.Service_name IN ('Close a policy', 'Upgrade a policy')
sql.E:
SELECT c.Customer_Name FROM Customers c
JOIN Customers_Policies cp ON c.Customer_ID = cp.Customer_ID
WHERE cp.Policy_ID IN (

question: Find the name and salary of instructors who are advisors of the students from the Math department.

sql.W1: SELECT T1.name, T1.salary FROM instructor AS T1 JOIN department AS T2 ON T1.dept_name = T2.dept_name WHERE T2.dept_name = 'Math' AND T1.dept_name = T1.name
sql.W2:
SELECT i.name, i.salary 
FROM instructor i
JOIN advisor a ON i.ID = a.i_ID
JOIN student s ON a.s_ID = s.ID
JOIN department d ON s.ID = d.dept_name
WHERE d.dept_name = 'Math'
sql.W3:

FROM instructor i
JOIN advisor a ON i.ID = a.i_ID
JOIN student s ON a.s_ID = s.ID
JOIN department d ON s.ID = d.dept_name
WHERE d.dept_name = 'Math'
sql.W4:
SELECT DISTINCT i.name, i.salary 
FROM instructor i 
JOIN advisor a ON i.ID = a.i_ID 
JOIN student s ON a.s_ID = s.ID 
JOIN department d ON s.dept_name = d.dept_name 
WHERE d.dept_name = 'Math'
sql.E: SELECT T1.name, T1.salary FROM instructor AS T1 JOIN advisor AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.i_ID JOIN student AS T3 ON T2.s_ID = T3.ID WHERE T1.dept_name = 'Math'

question: Find the name of amenities of the dorm where the student with last name Smith is living in.

sql.W1: SELECT T2.amenity_name FROM Dorm AS T1 JOIN Lives_in AS T3 ON T1.dormid = T3.dormid JOIN Student AS T4 ON T3.stuid = T4.StuID JOIN Dorm_amenities AS T5 ON T1.dormid = T5.dormid JOIN Amenities AS T2 ON T5.amenityid = T2.amenityid WHERE T4.last_name = 'Smith'
sql.W2:
SELECT D.dorm_name, DA.amenity_name 
FROM Dorm D
JOIN Lives_in LI ON D.dormid = LI.dormid
JOIN Has_amenity HA ON D.dormid = HA.dormid
JOIN Dorm_amenity DA ON HA.amenid = DA.amenid
JOIN Student S ON LI.stuid = S.StuID
WHERE S.LName = 'Smith'
sql.W3:
SELECT D.dorm_name, DA.amenity_name 
FROM Dorm D
JOIN Lives_in LI ON D.dormid = LI.dormid
JOIN Has_amenity HA ON D.dormid = HA.dormid
JOIN Dorm_amenity DA ON HA.amenid = DA.amenid
JOIN Student S ON LI.stuid = S.StuID
WHERE S.LName = 'Smith'
sql.W4:
SELECT da.amenity_name 
FROM Dorm_amenity da
JOIN Has_amenity ha ON da.amenid = ha.amenid
JOIN Dorm d ON ha.dormid = d.dormid
JOIN Lives_in li ON d.dormid = li.dormid
JOIN Student s ON li.stuid = s.StuID
WHERE s.LName = 'Smith'
sql.E: SELECT T2.amenity_name FROM Lives_in AS T1 JOIN Dorm AS T2 ON T1.dormid = T2.dormid JOIN Student AS T3 ON T1.stuid = T3.StuID WHERE T3.last_name = 'Smith'

question: What are the full names and cities of employees who have the letter Z in their first names?

sql.W1: SELECT FIRST_NAME || ' ' || LAST_NAME AS Full_Name, D.CITY FROM employees E JOIN departments D ON E.DEPARTMENT_ID = D.DEPARTMENT_ID WHERE FIRST_NAME LIKE '%Z%'
sql.W2: SELECT e.FIRST_NAME || ' ' || e.LAST_NAME AS Full_Name, d.LOCATION_ID FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.DEPARTMENT_ID = d.DEPARTMENT_ID WHERE e.FIRST_NAME LIKE '%Z%'
sql.W3: SELECT e.FIRST_NAME, e.LAST_NAME, d.LOCATION_ID FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.DEPARTMENT_ID = d.DEPARTMENT_ID WHERE e.FIRST_NAME LIKE '%Z%' AND d.LOCATION_ID IS NOT NULL
sql.W4: SELECT employees.FIRST_NAME, employees.LAST_NAME, locations.CITY FROM employees JOIN job_history ON employees.EMPLOYEE_ID = job_history.EMPLOYEE_ID JOIN departments ON employees.DEPARTMENT_ID = departments.DEPARTMENT_ID JOIN locations ON departments.LOCATION_ID = locations.LOCATION_ID WHERE employees.FIRST_NAME LIKE '%Z%'
sql.E:
SELECT e.FIRST_NAME || ' ' || e.LAST_NAME AS Full_Name, d.LOCATION_ID, l.CITY
FROM employees e
JOIN departments d ON e.DEPARTMENT_ID = d.DEPARTMENT_ID
JOIN job_history jh ON e.EMPLOYEE_ID = jh.EMPLOYEE_ID
JOIN locations l ON d.LOCATION_ID = l.LOCATION_ID
WHERE e.FIRST_NAME LIKE '%Z%'

question: Find the name of account that has the lowest total checking and saving balance.

sql.W1:
SELECT T1.name FROM ACCOUNTS AS T1 JOIN (
    SELECT custid, SUM(balance) AS total_balance
    FROM (
        SELECT custid, balance FROM CHECKING
        UNION ALL
        SELECT custid, balance FROM SAVINGS
    ) AS CombinedBalances
    GROUP BY custid
    ORDER BY total_balance ASC
    LIMIT 1
) AS T2 ON T1.custid = T2.custid
sql.W2: SELECT T2.name FROM SAVINGS AS T1 JOIN ACCOUNTS AS T2 ON T1.custid = T2.custid WHERE T1.balance + (SELECT MIN(balance) FROM SAVINGS) = T1.balance GROUP BY T2.name
sql.W3: SELECT T2.name FROM SAVINGS AS T1 JOIN ACCOUNTS AS T2 ON T1.custid = T2.custid WHERE T1.balance + (SELECT MIN(balance) FROM SAVINGS) = T1.balance GROUP BY T2.name
sql.W4: SELECT T1.name FROM ACCOUNTS AS T1 JOIN CHECKING AS T2 ON T1.custid = T2.custid JOIN SAVINGS AS T3 ON T1.custid = T3.custid WHERE T2.balance + T3.balance = (SELECT MIN(T2.balance + T3.balance) FROM CHECKING AS T2 JOIN SAVINGS AS T3 ON T1.custid = T2.custid)
sql.E:
SELECT T1.name FROM ACCOUNTS AS T1 JOIN (
    SELECT custid, SUM(balance) AS total_balance
    FROM (
        SELECT custid, balance FROM CHECKING
        UNION ALL
        SELECT custid, balance FROM SAVINGS
    ) AS CombinedBalances
    GROUP BY custid
    ORDER BY total_balance ASC
    LIMIT 1
) AS T2 ON T1.custid = T2.custid

question: List the names of all the distinct customers who bought a keyboard.

FROM Customers c 
JOIN Customer_Orders co ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id

       (SELECT s.supplier_name

              co2.order

       (SELECT s.supplier_name

              co2.order

JOIN Customer_Orders co ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id

question: What are the average fastest lap speed in races held after 2004 grouped by race name and ordered by year?

sql.W1:
SELECT r.year, AVG(l.milliseconds / 100) AS avg_fastest_lap_speed
FROM lapTimes l
JOIN races r ON l.raceId = r.raceId
WHERE r.year > 2004
GROUP BY r.year, r.name
ORDER BY r.year
sql.W2:
SELECT r.name, AVG(fastestLapSpeed) AS avg_fastest_lap_speed
FROM races r
JOIN results res ON r.raceId = res.raceId
JOIN drivers d ON res.driverId = d.driverId
WHERE r.year > 2004
GROUP BY r.name
ORDER BY r.year
sql.W3:
SELECT r.name, AVG(fastestLapSpeed) AS avg_fastest_lap_speed
FROM races r
JOIN results res ON r.raceId = res.raceId
JOIN lapTimes lt ON res.resultId = lt.resultId
WHERE r.year > 2004
GROUP BY r.name
ORDER BY r.year
sql.W4:
SELECT r.name, AVG(rs.fastestLapSpeed) AS avg_fastest_lap_speed
FROM races r
JOIN results rs ON r.raceId = rs.raceId
WHERE r.year > 2004
GROUP BY r.name
ORDER BY r.year
sql.E:
SELECT r.name, AVG(fastestLapSpeed) AS avg_fastest_lap_speed
FROM races r
JOIN results res ON r.raceId = res.raceId
JOIN pitStops ps ON res.resultId = ps.driverId AND res.raceId = ps.raceId
JOIN (
    SELECT raceId, MAX(millisecond) AS max_millisecond
    FROM pitStops
    GROUP BY raceId
) ps_max ON ps.race

question: How many players were in the team Boston Red Stockings in 2000?

sql.W2:

sql.W4:

JOIN postseason o ON t.team_id = o.team_id_winner OR t.team_id = o.team_id_loser 
JOIN player p ON p.player_id = t.team_id 
WHERE t.year = 2000 AND t.name = 'Boston Red Stockings'
sql.E:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.player_id) 
FROM batting AS T1 
JOIN team AS T2 ON T1.team_id = T2.team_id 
JOIN team_franchise AS T3 ON T2.franchise_id = T3.franchise_id 
WHERE T2.name = 'Boston Red Stockings' AND T1.year = 2000

question: find the name and age of the pilot who has won the most number of times among the pilots who are younger than 30.

sql.W1: SELECT Name, Age FROM pilot WHERE Age < 30 ORDER BY (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM win WHERE Win_Pilot_Id = Pilot.Pilot_Id) DESC LIMIT 1
sql.W2:
SELECT p.Name, p.Age 
FROM pilot p 
JOIN match m ON p.Pilot_Id = m.Winning_Pilot 
WHERE p.Age < 30 
GROUP BY p.Pilot_Id 
HAVING COUNT(m.Round) = (SELECT MAX(win_count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(Round) AS win_count, Winning_Pilot FROM match GROUP BY Winning_Pilot))

This query selects the names and ages of pilots who are younger than 30 and have won
sql.W3:
SELECT p.Name, p.Age 
FROM pilot p 
JOIN match m ON p.Pilot_Id = m.Winning_Pilot 
WHERE p.Age < 30 
GROUP BY p.Pilot_Id 
HAVING COUNT(m.Round) = (SELECT MAX(win_count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(Round) AS win_count, Winning_Pilot FROM match GROUP BY Winning_Pilot))

This query selects the names and ages of pilots who are younger than 30 and have won
sql.W4:
SELECT p.Name, p.Age 
FROM pilot p 
JOIN match m ON p.Pilot_Id = m.Winning_Pilot 
GROUP BY p.Pilot_Id 
HAVING COUNT(m.Round) = (
    SELECT MAX(wins) 
    FROM (
        SELECT COUNT(Round) AS wins 
        FROM match 
        JOIN pilot ON match.Winning_Pilot = pilot.Pilot_Id
